encoder: a single Sonnet 5.5 agent working alone from the brief (BRIEF.md); no subagents
display_name: Sale of Goods Act 1979 (Singapore; the Act applied from England): isomorphic layer-1 modules and a buyer's seat layer, target main
license: The quoted source text carries the terms in SOURCE-LICENSE.md (which points at the subject-level note). No licence for the encoding itself was set by the encoder.
seat: a buyer of goods under a contract of sale in Singapore, asking on facts they can state what terms are implied, when the property and the risk pass, what they may do if the goods are late, defective or not as described, and what they owe the seller

scope.edition: Sale of Goods Act 1979, Singapore, 2020 Revised Edition, informal consolidation, version in force from 1/4/2022 (a converter's plain-text rendering, not the official text)
scope.encoded: ss 1 to 62 except ss 22, 40 and 58 (not applicable or omitted); the 17 defined terms of s 61(1) and the rules of reading in s 61(2) to (5); the Schedule, paragraphs 1 to 6 and 9 to 13 (paragraphs 7 and 8 are deleted in the text)
scope.not_encoded: the title, long title, Part headings, arrangement of sections, the Legislative History, key to abbreviations and comparative table (inert, reasons 1 and 2); s 63, the short title (inert, reason 2); the borrowed terms and the judgments the Act hands to the court, which are inputs

not_reviewed: No domain expert has read this encoding against the text, and the text it was written from is a converter's plain-text rendering, not the official text. The Hohfeld kinds, the marginal readings and the forks are the encoder's, not a lawyer's.
